editorial:
Imagine being a kid who loves scary stories so much that you actually get kidnapped by a witch. That is exactly what happens to Alex, a lonely boy who finds himself locked in a magic apartment in New York City. The vibe is like a spooky fairy tale mixed with a modern city setting. You get to see Alex face off against a witch who forces him to write a new terrifying story every night just to stay alive. It is a great mix of creepy moments and funny bits that make the whole experience feel like a dark ride at a theme park.

The acting is top-notch, especially the witch who is both scary and weirdly funny. The way the stories come to life on screen is a huge plus, and the pacing keeps you moving quickly toward the finish line. While some of the CGI looks a bit too digital, the heart of the story makes up for it. It is a perfect pick for anyone who likes a bit of a chill down their spine without being too traumatizing.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Alex realizes the witch is just as lonely as he is. Instead of trying to outsmart her with a scary story, he writes a tale about friendship and forgiveness. This kindness breaks the witch's heart in a good way, causing her to let him and the other kids go. The magic of the apartment fades, and Alex returns home with a new sense of confidence and some new friends.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy stories and magic.
